_comment: Octail's own egg (plan §6.4): runs any executable JAR (java -jar) on Java 8 to 25, the heap (-Xmx) a share of the server's memory so the JVM's own overhead fits under the limit. The JAR is uploaded or downloaded at install from an https:// address, optionally checked against its SHA-256.
name: Java App (JAR)
author: octail@meowgafactory.com
description: Any Java app packaged as an executable JAR: bots (JDA, Javacord), Spring Boot services, small tools. Upload the JAR or have the install download it; it runs with java -jar, its heap sized from the server's memory.

startup_commands.Default:
if [ ! -f "${JAR_FILE}" ]; then echo "[Octail] ${JAR_FILE} wasn't found: upload the JAR, or set JAR Download URL and reinstall"; exit 1; fi; octail_app() { java $([ "{{SERVER_MEMORY}}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && printf -- '-Xmx%sM' "$(( {{SERVER_MEMORY}} * {{HEAP_PERCENT}} / 100 ))") ${JAVA_ARGS} -jar "${JAR_FILE}" ${APP_ARGS}; }; if [ -z "${READY_TEXT}" ]; then printf '[Octail] App is %s
' running; octail_app; else set -o pipefail; octail_app 2>&1 | { while IFS= read -r l || [ -n "$l" ]; do printf '%s
' "$l"; case "$l" in *"${READY_TEXT}"*) printf '[Octail] App is %s
' running; break;; esac; done; exec cat; }; fi

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Octail Java JAR install: downloads the JAR from JAR Download URL when one is set (its SHA-256 checked when JAR
# SHA-256 is set); without one the server stays empty for an upload. Other files in the folder are kept.
#
# Server Files: /mnt/server
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

if [ -z "${JAR_URL:-}" ]; then
    echo "No download address set: upload your JAR as ${JAR_FILE} with the file manager or SFTP."
    exit 0
fi
case "${JAR_URL}" in
    https://*) ;;
    *)
        echo "Installation failed: JAR Download URL must be an https:// address."
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

mkdir -p "$(dirname "${JAR_FILE}")"
echo "Downloading ${JAR_URL}"
if ! curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --retry 3 -o "${JAR_FILE}.download" "${JAR_URL}"; then
    rm -f "${JAR_FILE}.download"
    echo "Installation failed: the download didn't work."
    exit 1
fi
if [ -n "${JAR_SHA256:-}" ]; then
    if ! echo "${JAR_SHA256}  ${JAR_FILE}.download" | sha256sum -c --quiet -; then
        rm -f "${JAR_FILE}.download"
        echo "Installation failed: the download doesn't match JAR SHA-256."
        exit 1
    fi
else
    echo "No JAR SHA-256 set; the download isn't checked."
fi
mv -f "${JAR_FILE}.download" "${JAR_FILE}"

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed: ${JAR_FILE}"
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: JAR File
variables.description: The JAR to run, relative to the server folder.

variables.name: JAR Download URL
variables.description: Optional: an https:// address the install downloads the JAR from (a GitHub release asset, your build server). Empty: upload the JAR yourself. Reinstall to download again.

variables.name: JAR SHA-256
variables.description: Optional: the SHA-256 checksum of the download; the install fails when it differs.

variables.name: Heap Share
variables.description: The share of the server's memory given to the Java heap (-Xmx), in percent. The rest is left for the JVM itself; lower it if the server is killed for memory.

variables.name: Java Options
variables.description: Extra JVM flags before -jar, such as -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 or -XX:+UseZGC.

variables.name: App Arguments
variables.description: Extra arguments passed to the app, split at spaces.

variables.name: Ready Text
variables.description: Console text that means the app is up, such as 'Logged in as'. The server shows Running once a line contains it (or once the app listens on the main port). Empty: Running as soon as the app starts.
